threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still queue for the bus like it's a polite London thing, not just a suggestion. Locals just know when to assert their place.
Last night on the 109, a guy argued his vinyl collection was worth more than the bus fare. The driver just shook his head and kept driving.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy in a full suit, clutching a falafel wrap, hopping on the U-Bahn with a massive dog—only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop that serves late-night vegan döner with curry sauce – a local secret that beats the conventional options.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here when they can name the taco truck at 16th and Mission by the sound of the blender alone.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today with a live saxophonist jammin' by the back door—only in the Tenderloin do you get a free concert with your commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all bars close at 2 AM, but real locals know the best ones stay open till sunrise, especially around Plaça del Sol.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by the way they hesitate at tram stops, clearly studying the map like it’s a treasure map. It's the telltale sign!

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look shocked when you hear a tube strike's on. The locals just nod and carry on, like it's the weather.
Got on the 36 last night and a bloke was deep into a heated debate with a bag of chips. The chips won, but he didn't even flinch. Classic Peckham.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I found someone selling homemade Mutzen on the corner every Saturday, just like my grandma used to. It feels like a real community.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find abandoned subway stations here, like
Pankstraße: - hidden gems where you can still feel the city's history.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their disdain for the BART delays—when the train's late, we know to grab tacos first, then check for updates.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy at the Muni stop trying to trade his skateboard for coffee. The barista looked confused, but hey, it’s San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia’s park benches are for picnics; locals know they’re for people-watching, especially during the evening hours.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their eagerness to ask for directions at every turn, even when the Metro entrance is just steps away.
